evidence.api_compatibility: No API impact. The change is confined to .github/workflows/cpp_server_build_test_release.yml and only alters when inference backend jobs execute within the CI pipeline.
evidence.documentation: No documentation updates needed. This is an internal CI optimization with no user-facing behavior change.
evidence.manual_release_testing: This is a CI-only change that affects internal build infrastructure. It does not ship any user-visible artifact, CLI command, API endpoint, or GUI behavior. No manual release testing is required.
evidence.post_approval_commits: None. The single commit (f748f4fff4746f1b1fbb775ff465ae9f548b0d32) predates the approval by @superm1 at 2026-09-16T19:34:18Z. No commits were added after approval.
evidence.review: PR #3604 was reviewed and approved by @superm1, a subject-matter expert in CI and Linux packaging per docs/dev/contribute.md. The approval review included a tangential comment about adding cherry-pick line checks on release branches; the author redirected that discussion to a separate issue. The review was substantive and appropriate for the change.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The change adds a benign branch-matching condition to skip expensive build jobs. No credential handling, network calls, code execution, or dependency changes.
evidence.tests: No new feature code; this is a workflow condition change (3 lines added). The change is verified by CI running on the merge group, where all checks passed: C++ Server Build/Test/Release (including the modified workflow, inference backend jobs correctly ran on main), CodeQL, Docs And Style, Launchpad PPA, and all validation workflows. The condition logic is self-evident — adding a branch prefix check is functionally correct by inspection.

subject: Don't run inference backend jobs on release branch builds (#3604)
summary: Skips inference backend build/test jobs in the release workflow when triggered from release-v branches.
verdict_reason: A minimal, well-scoped CI fix with proper reviewer expertise, passing all checks, and no user-visible surface requiring release testing.
